actions.diff:
--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -305,2 +305,33 @@
-    digest = sha256(sha256(v).digest()).digest()
-    return b58encode(v + digest[:4], alphabet)
+    digest = sha256(sha256(v).digest()).digest()
+    v += digest[:4]
+
+    # Same steps as b58encode, inlined to save a call per encode
+    origlen = len(v)
+    v = v.lstrip(b'\0')
+    newlen = len(v)
+    i = int.from_bytes(v, 'big')
+    tables = _encode_tables.get(alphabet)
+    if tables is None:
+        return b58encode(digest[:0].join((b'\0' * (origlen - newlen), v)),
+                         alphabet)
+    pairs, sq, big, big3, zero = tables
+    parts = []
+    while i >= big3:
+        i, rem = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem2 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem3 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem4 = divmod(i, big)
+        parts += (pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq],
+                  pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem3 % sq], pairs[rem3 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem4 % sq], pairs[rem4 // sq])
+    if i >= big:
+        i, rem = divmod(i, big)
+        rem3, rem2 = divmod(i, big)
+        parts += (pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq],
+                  pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem3 % sq], pairs[rem3 // sq])
+    elif i:
+        parts += pairs[i % sq], pairs[i // sq]
+    parts.reverse()
+    return zero * (origlen - newlen) + b''.join(parts).lstrip(zero)

+    # Same steps as b58decode, inlined to save a call per decode once the

+        digits = v.translate(table)
+        if 255 in digits:
+            bad = v[digits.index(255)]
+            raise ValueError("Invalid character {!r}".format(chr(bad)))
+        acc = int.from_bytes(digits, 'big')
+        merge = merges[(len(digits) - 1).bit_length()]
+        if merge is None:
+            result = b58decode(v, alphabet, autofix=autofix)
+            result = b'\0' * (origlen - newlen) + result
+        else:
+            steps, last_shift, last_factor = merge
+            for shift, mask, factor in steps:
+                acc -= (acc >> shift & mask) * factor
+            acc -= (acc >> last_shift) * last_factor
+            result = acc.to_bytes(
+                origlen - newlen + (acc.bit_length() + 7) // 8, 'big')

journal.text:
Test agent here. Session on base58-py. The bar was a 1% drop in check_ir with the same bytes out.

First I inlined the b58encode and b58decode bodies into the two check functions. Equivalence held. It was rejected. check_ir ratio 1.0120, encode_ir 1.0171, decode_ir 1.0159. The 63 added lines cost about 3.7M instructions at module load. That beat roughly 1.6M saved by skipping 2000 calls. Then I routed b58decode_int's table path through b58decode to drop the duplicated lane. Also rejected. check_ir ratio 0.9983 against a required 0.9900. Outputs identical both times. I submitted no candidate.

What I believe now: in this bench, module load counts. Extra lines are not free. Saved call overhead is small next to the load cost of new code. Deleting duplication helps, but only a little.

Next I will look for a change that removes code and also cuts work per character inside the divmod loop. I will read lineage_bench.py again first to see where the instructions go.
